Henceforth the world’s first workers’ state could present itself, and was often perceived by others, as the polar opposite of fascism and hence as the world’s only unwavering antifascist force. For the Left generally, fascism stood for absolute evil, and so Communism

was cast in the role of the indispensable guardian of good. Thus, from the mid-thirties onward the old principle of “no enemies to the Left” was given a new, more radical meaning. Liberals seemed summoned by history to the perilous policy of allying with the antiliberal Left against the new ultra-Right.

zh: 的确，把一般法西斯主义视为帝国主义新面孔的概念，是共产主义者的创造。（法西斯列强自己直到1937年后缔结政治同盟时，才认为它们构成一个共同运动。）法西斯主义作为一个一般术语，最早由共产国际在1922年墨索里尼上台时提出，并很快发展成一种普遍理论，把政治法西斯主义视为“金融资本”的幌子。因此它现成地可用于解释希特勒的夺权，此后又可用于把任何反共力量定性为法西斯主义的一个变种，正如三十年代初共产党人把社会民主党人称为“社会法西斯分子”。根据这种一般法西斯主义理论，激进反法西斯主义成为全世界共产主义鼓动的中心主题。因此，1935年后，反法西斯人民阵线是苏联在国际事务中的主要王牌，也是把共产主义影响广泛传播到工人阶级以外的工具。
en: Indeed, the concept of generic fascism as the new face of imperialism was a Communist creation. (The fascist powers themselves did not think that they constituted a common movement until they formed political alliances after 1937.) Fascism as a generic term was first put forward by the Comintern in 1922 on Mussolini’s accession to power, and was soon elaborated into a general theory whereby political fascism was seen as a front for “finance capital.” It was thus ready-made to explain Hitler’s seizure of power, and thereafter to characterize any anti-Communist force as a species of fascism, as when Communists in the early thirties labeled Social Democrats “social fascists.” On the basis of this generic theory of fascism, militant antifascism became the central theme of Communist agitation throughout the world. Thus, after 1935 the antifascist Popular Front was the Soviet Union’s principal trump in international affairs and the means of spreading Communist influence far beyond the working class.

zh: 但由于斯大林寻求这种影响是为了增进苏联安全，而不是促进外国革命，从1935年起，“反法西斯斗争”总是与“争取和平的斗争”联系在一起。因此，斯大林并不准备采取多少具体行动来打击法西斯主义，因为对西方革命的任何支持都会疏远他在对付希特勒时可能需要借重的资产阶级列强——法国和英国。同样重要的是，苏联对国外反法西斯斗争的任何重大介入，都会危及仍然不稳的苏维埃国家。因此对斯大林来说，西班牙与其说是机会，不如说是危险。苏联对西班牙事务的介入，较少是为了支持共和国，更多是为了防止它陷入社会主义革命；而内务人民委员部在西班牙清算托洛茨基分子的无情程度，与它在俄国所做的一样。
en: But since this influence was sought by Stalin to further Soviet security rather than to promote foreign revolution, from 1935 onward the “struggle against fascism” was always coupled with the “struggle for peace.” Consequently, Stalin was not prepared to do much in a concrete way to combat fascism, for any support of revolution in the West would alienate the bourgeois powers—France and England—that he might need against Hitler. Just as important, any significant Soviet involvement in the antifascist struggle abroad would endanger the still-shaky Soviet state. Hence for Stalin, Spain was not so much an opportunity as a danger. Soviet involvement in Spanish affairs was directed less at supporting the republic than at preventing it from falling into socialist revolution; and the NKVD liquidated the Trotskyites in Spain as ruthlessly as it did those in Russia.

zh: 在这种情况下，党的反帝国主义和反法西斯传统，对正在通过清洗进行巩固的苏联党国来说，变得危险起来。然而，这些传统自1928年以来一直是党的辞令中刺耳的常用语，当时斯大林在国际事务中开创了“阶级对阶级”的激进左翼政策，与他在国内发动的阶级斗争相呼应。而且，这种辞令符合许多党员更深的情绪，他们毕竟在情感上仍属左翼。把人民阵线字面理解为反法西斯革命主义，不仅吸引党内残存的托洛茨基分子；布哈林和图哈切夫斯基元帅等人物也表达了这种看法。在这个问题上，苏联内部“右派”与“左派”的区分不再成立。在国际危机中，党内这种不加思考的左翼情绪，可能把苏维埃国家推向危险的外国纠葛。因此，最好在世界形势变得更糟之前消除这类倾向，在外交和国内事务上都只保留一个权威中心——同时让不受过时左翼口号束缚的新人来服从这一权威。清洗最终始于国际上具有关键意义的1936年夏天，这大概并非偶然。
en: Under such circumstances the anti-imperialist and antifascist traditions of the Party came to appear perilous to the Soviet Party-state, which was then in the process of consolidation through purge. Yet these traditions had been the strident staple of Party rhetoric ever since 1928, when Stalin inaugurated the militant Leftist policy of “class against class” in international affairs as the pendant to his class warfare at home. This rhetoric, moreover, corresponded to the deeper sentiments of many members of the Party, who remained, after all, emotionally on the Left. A literal interpretation of the Popular Front as antifascist revolutionism appealed not only to residual Trotskyites within the Party; it was also voiced by such figures as Bukharin and Marshal Tukhachevskii. On this issue the internal Soviet division between “Right” and “Left” ceased to hold. In an international crisis such unthinking Leftist sentiment within the Party might push the Soviet state towards dangerous foreign entanglements. It would be better, therefore, to eliminate such tendencies before the world situation got any worse, and to have only one center of authority in foreign as in domestic matters—as well as new men unencumbered by outmoded Leftist slogans to obey this authority. It is probably no accident that the purge finally began in the internationally pivotal summer of 1936.

zh: 尽管如此，政变必须从一个具体问题启动，即在党内未受足够惩罚的反对派仍然存在；自1932年留京事件（也许还有同年一个小型托洛茨基小组的成立）以来，这件事一直令斯大林耿耿于怀。斯大林此时重新提起此事的另一个原因，可能是希特勒已经提供了一个成功血洗的先例：1934年6月，他在“长刀之夜”中清除了恩斯特·罗姆及其冲锋队。据一位身居要职的内务人民委员部叛逃者说，斯大林在一次政治局会议上以钦佩的口吻评论了这一行动。斯大林还断言，希特勒的政变使纳粹主义从革命阶段进入国家建设阶段，并宣称苏联革命也该进行同样的过渡了。
因此，为完成苏维埃国家建设的过程，斯大林再次着手打破党内禁止死刑的禁忌。
en: Still, the coup d’état had to take off from a specific issue, namely, the persistence of inadequately punished opposition within the Party; this was a matter that had not ceased to fester in Stalin’s mind since the Riutin affair in 1932 (and perhaps since the creation of a small Trotskyite group the same year). Another reason why Stalin may have returned to the matter at this time is that Hitler had already given an example of a successful blood purge when, in June 1934, he liquidated Ernst Roehm and his SA troops in the Night of the Long Knives. According to a well-placed NKVD defector, Stalin commented on this action with admiration in a Politburo meeting. Stalin also asserted that Hitler’s coup had moved Nazism from its revolutionary to its state-building phase, and he declared that it was time the Soviet Revolution made the same transition.
So to cap off the process of Soviet state-building, Stalin once again moved to break the Party taboo against the death penalty within its ranks.

zh: 斯大林选择季诺维也夫和加米涅夫作为第一批受害者，他们是旧反对派中最脆弱的人。这两人已被开除出党并悔过；的确，他们多次进出监狱，作为政治人物已彻底名誉扫地。审判的公式——供认导致死刑判决——可追溯到沙赫特事件（其实还可追溯到1922年对社会革命党人的审判）；就连检察官安德烈·维辛斯基也是同一个人。于是1936年8月，斯大林把季诺维也夫、加米涅夫和其他十四人送上被告席，指控他们组织了一个“托洛茨基—季诺维也夫恐怖中心”，杀害了基洛夫，并密谋刺杀斯大林和政治局大多数成员，据称这一切都是为了在德国和日本法西斯帮助下复辟资本主义。
en: Stalin chose as his first victims Zinoviev and Kamenev, the most vulnerable of the old oppositionists. These two had already been expelled from the Party and had recanted; indeed, they had been in and out of jail so many times that they were thoroughly discredited as political figures. The formula for the trial—confessions leading to death sentences—went back to the Shakhty affair (and indeed to the trial of the Socialist Revolutionaries in 1922); even the prosecutor, Andrei Vyshinskii, was the same. So in August 1936 Stalin put Zinoviev, Kamenev, and fourteen others in the dock and accused them of having formed a “Trotskyite-Zinovievite terrorist center” that murdered Kirov and conspired to assassinate Stalin and most of the Politburo, all with the alleged purpose of restoring capitalism with the aid of German and Japanese fascists.

〔译注〕沙赫特案的审判长是维辛斯基，公诉人是克雷连科；维辛斯基后来担任1936年莫斯科审判的公诉人。

zh: 然而，这场审判搞砸了。看来内务人民委员部首脑、审判的组织者亚戈达不情愿地执行了他厌恶的命令。关于反对派在西方与托洛茨基之子会面的证据明显是伪造的，西方媒体立即指出了这一点。尽管“罪人”当然供认并被判处死刑，这场表演的教育效果还是被破坏了。于是斯大林着手建立一个更顺从的内务人民委员部来组织新的审判。9月25日，他和日丹诺夫在黑海索契度假时，向政治局发电报说，必须紧急用斯大林私人秘书处成员尼古拉·叶若夫取代亚戈达。他们给出的换人理由是，政治警察在“揭露托洛茨基—季诺维也夫集团”方面“落后了四年”——这一时间跨度显然把事情追溯到1932年的留京事件。正是这一行动把清洗变成了政变。随后，政变在1936年9月季诺维也夫和加米涅夫审判与1937年6月苏联元帅们被处决之间，以惊人的速度展开。
en: The trial, however, was botched. It seems that Yagoda, the head of the NKVD and the trial’s organizer, carried out his distasteful orders with reluctance. Evidence concerning meetings in the West between oppositionists and Trotsky’s son was palpably false, and this was immediately pointed out in the Western press. Although the “guilty” of course confessed and were duly condemned to death, the pedagogical effect of the performance was nonetheless spoiled. Stalin therefore proceeded to create a more submisive NKVD to organize new trials. On September 25 he and Zhdanov, while on vacation at Sochi on the Black Sea, sent a telegram to the Politburo saying it was urgent to replace Yagoda with a member of Stalin’s personal secretariat, Nikolai Ezhov. The reason they gave for this change was that the political police was “four years behind” in “unmasking the TrotskyiteZinovievite bloc”—a time span that clearly took matters back to the Riutin affair in 1932. It is this action that turned the purge into a coup d’état. The coup then unfolded with stunning rapidity between the September 1936 trial of Zinoviev and Kamenev and the execution of the Soviet marshals in June 1937.

〔译注〕本段前文所述季诺维也夫和加米涅夫的公开审判于1936年8月进行；此处原书写为9月。

zh: 第一步是把内务人民委员部置于斯大林的直接控制之下。该机构当然从来不是独立机构，但在从捷尔任斯基到亚戈达历任首脑之下，它享有相对的专业自主和团体认同感。这一局面随叶若夫的任命而结束：这个被称为“机关”的安全机器规模大增，其主要使命此时是充当斯大林对付党的武器。于是斯大林把自己的个人控制范围，从他在二十年代征服的党，扩展到他在1930年接管的政府，再扩展到普遍监控系统即政治警察。
en: The first step was to bring the NKVD under Stalin’s direct control. That agency, of course, had never been an independent body, but under a succession of directors, from Dzerzhinskii to Yagoda, it had enjoyed a relative professional autonomy and sense of corporate identity. This situation ended with Ezhov’s appointment: The “organs,” as the security apparatus was called, grew greatly in size, and their chief mission now was to serve as Stalin’s weapon against the Party. Stalin thus expanded his sphere of personal control from the Party, which he had conquered in the 1920s, to the government, which he had taken over in 1930, to the universal monitoring system, the political police.

zh: 第二步是修补1936年8月审判造成的损害。办法是对余下的旧反对派进行新的、万无一失的审判。许多被告，包括前左翼分子尤里·皮亚塔科夫以及布哈林和李可夫，都已在第一次审判的证词中被牵连。但看来中央委员会内部再次出现了反对彻底清除旧反对派的阻力，而这三人都是中央委员。这种态度既表达了对党的稳定的关切，也表达了其干部此时已获得的团体认同感。结果是妥协：斯大林放弃了对两位右派的指控，但在1937年1月，他以惯常的罪名——从刺杀基洛夫到在法西斯纵容下复辟资本主义——审判并判处皮亚塔科夫和“托洛茨基中心”另外十五名成员死刑。
en: The second step was to repair the damage done by the August 1936 trial. This was done by staging new, foolproof trials of remaining old oppositionists. Many of the defendants, including the former Leftist Iurii Piatakov as well as Bukharin and Rykov, had been implicated in testimony at the first trial. But it seems there was again resistance within the Central Committee, where these three sat, to a clean sweep of old oppositionists. This attitude expressed both a concern for the Party’s stability and a sense of corporate identity its cadres had by now acquired. The result was a compromise: Stalin backed off from accusing the two Rightists, hut in January 1937 he tried and condemned to death Piatakov and fifteen other members of a “Trotskyite Center” on the usual accusations, from assassinating Kirov to restoring capitalism with fascist connivance.

zh: 与此同时，一项新罪名被提出：工业破坏，这意味着通过皮亚塔科夫——他曾是苏联工业化的头脑——全国整个管理干部队伍都受到威胁。但这使斯大林与他一些最亲密的支持者发生冲突，最著名的是皮亚塔科夫的上级奥尔忠尼启则，他显然反对说，清洗的这一延伸危及整个制度。这场冲突导致一场激烈的争吵和1937年1月奥尔忠尼启则的自杀（还是谋杀？）。这一事件使斯大林确信，政变必须走到底，清除一切可能抵抗他绝对集中统治的角落。
en: At the same time a new crime was charged: industrial wrecking, which meant that through Piatakov, who had been the brains of Soviet industrialization, the whole managerial corps of the country was threatened. But this brought Stalin into conflict with some of his own closest supporters, most notably Piatakov’s superior, Ordzhonikidze, who apparently objected that this extension of the purge imperiled the whole system. This conflict led to a violet quarrel and Ordzhonikidze’s suicide (or murder?) in January of 1937. And this event convinced Stalin that the coup had to go all the way and clean out every potential pocket of resistance to his absolute, centralized rule.

〔译注〕有关资料通常将奥尔忠尼启则死亡时间记为1937年2月18日；死亡方式存在争议，本书写作1月。

zh: 政变在1937年2—3月中央委员会的一场旷日持久的会议上达到顶点。

在激烈的辩论中，斯大林、叶若夫和莫洛托夫压倒了主张温和的人——后者显然大多与新重工业有关——终于使布哈林和李可夫落入手中，二人在会议期间被捕（他们从前的同事托姆斯基在1936年8月审判中被牵连后已自杀）。1938年3月，布哈林、李可夫和被废黜的内务人民委员部首脑亚戈达，连同另外十八人，作为“右派和托洛茨基分子反苏联盟”因惯常的万国阴谋受审。尽管由于被告的身份，这是最著名的一场审判，但到它发生时，它已是政变的尾声，而不是核心。
en: The coup culminated in a protracted meeting of the Central Committee in February-March 1937.

In stormy debates, Stalin, Ezhov, and Molotov faced down the advocates of moderation, most of whom were apparently connected with the new heavy industry, and obtained at last the heads of Bukharin and Rykov, who were arrested during the session (their erstwhile colleague, Tomskii, had committed suicide after being implicated in the August 1936 trial). In March of 1938, Bukharin, Rykov, and the deposed NKVD chief Yagoda, together with eighteen others, were tried for the usual universal conspiracy as an “Anti-Soviet Bloc of Rights and Trotskyites.” Although this was the most famous of the trials—given the personalities of the defendants—by the time it occurred it was an epilogue rather than the centerpiece of the coup.

zh: 政变的真正顶点在1937年6月到来。在斯大林于1936年8月审判至1937年2—3月全会之间把内务人民委员部放出来对付党之后，只剩下一个机构可能采取行动反对他：军队。的确，他对党和工业管理者的攻击，第一次给武装力量提供了一个可能的动机，去废黜一个他们很可能觉得此时已危及整个制度的领袖——正如奥尔忠尼启则早先所感觉的那样——而且是在国际形势升温之时。即便比斯大林更少疑心的人，也有理由保护自己的军事侧翼。此外，军队虽然被干部职务名称表制度覆盖，却像政治警察一样拥有相对自主的传统和可追溯到内战的职业团体精神。此外，它由那部史诗的一批在世英雄领导，其中最著名的是图哈切夫斯基元帅。
en: The real culmination of the coup came in June of 1937. After Stalin had unleashed the NKVD on the Party between the August 1936 trial and the February-March plenum, there remained only one institution that might possibly act against him: the army. Indeed, his attack on the Party and the industrial managers for the first time gave the armed forces a possible motive for deposing a leader who they might well feel now endangered the whole system—as Ordzhonikidze had felt earlier—and at a time when the international situation was heating up. Even a less suspicious person than Stalin would have reason to protect himself on his military flank. The army, moreover, though covered by the

system, possessed, like the political police, a tradition of relative autonomy and a professional esprit de corps going back to the Civil War. In addition, it was led by a number of living heroes of that epic, the most prominent of whom was Marshal Tukhachevskii.

zh: 鉴于这个群体的潜在力量，斯大林毫不迟疑地为这些（在他看来）可能危险的人物安排了一场作秀式审判；而这些人本来也很可能不会配合这样一场闹剧。图哈切夫斯基和其他六名元帅、将军被即席秘密审判，随即枪决。公众只是在一则简短公告中披露该群体的“叛国”时，才知道这场政变。但这些武器精良的人为什么如此轻易地屈服？鉴于他们事先已有所察觉，这个问题尤其切题；因为在之前几周，斯大林已把其中一些人降职，他们看到他零敲碎打地这样处置皮亚塔科夫、亚戈达和许多其他人。唯一的答案只能是：他们不仅是军事英雄，而且——其实首先是——党的干部；像他们从前的指挥官托洛茨基、皮亚塔科夫以及许多其他人一样，他们知道没有人能反对党而正确。于是制度中最后一个半自主领域——军队——被压制了，连一声呜咽都没发出。
en: Given the potential power of this group, Stalin wasted no time in contriving a show trial for these (to him) potentially dangerous men, who might well not have cooperated anyway in such a farce. Tukhachevskii and six other marshals and generals were summarily tried in camera and immediately shot. The public learned about this coup only when the group’s “treason” was revealed in a terse public announcement. But why did these well-armed men submit so easily? The question is especially pertinent in view of the fact that they had some warning of what was coming; for Stalin had demoted a number of them in the previous weeks, a piecemeal degradation they had seen him practice on Piatakov, Yagoda, and so many others. The only answer can be that they were not just military heroes, but also—indeed, above all—Party men, and like their erstwhile commander Trotsky, Piatakov, and so many others, they knew that no one could be right against the Party. So the last area of semiautonomy in the system, the military, was suppressed without it emitting so much as a whimper.

〔译注〕1937年6月的秘密军事审判中，图哈切夫斯基与另外7名高级军官共8人受审；本书写作另外6人。

zh: 苏联的一切权力此时都集中于一个人：斯大林已成为“独裁者”，取的是这个古老罗马和共和词汇被扭曲的现代含义。2—3月中央全会和对高级军官的审判，实际上打断了所有实际或潜在抵抗斯大林的脊梁。政变此时已在最高层完成；从这时起直到斯大林去世，党的宪政遗迹停止运作。于是通向深度政变的道路打开了，那场在党各级大规模更换人员的行动，正是斯大林自1932年以来一直摸索着要做的。每一次阻挠这一愿望的努力——无论是基洛夫的、亚戈达的、古比雪夫的还是奥尔忠尼启则的——都只是成功地点燃了斯大林的激情。因此，1937年3月之后直到1938年底，叶若夫时期的大恐怖畅通无阻地展开。
en: All power in the Soviet Union now culminated in a single man: Stalin had become “dictator” in the perverted modern meaning of that venerable Roman and republican word. The February-March Central Committee plenum and the trial of senior military officers had effectively broken the back of all actual or potential resistance to Stalin. The coup had now been completed at the highest levels; from this time and until Stalin’s death the vestiges of Party constitutionalism ceased to operate. The way was thus open for the coup-in-depth, that great sweep of personnel, at all levels of the Party, towards which Stalin had been groping since 1932. Every effort to thwart this desire—whether it was Kirov’s, Yagoda’s, Kuibyshev’s, or Ordzhonikidze’s—had only succeeded in stoking Stalin’s passion. After March 1937, therefore, and until the end of 1938, the Great Terror of the
unfolded without let or hindrance.

zh: 斯大林在最高层监督这一行动，并经常与其他政治局成员一起签署要清除的人员名单。但实际执行清洗的是叶若夫及其内务人民委员部幕僚，他们在决定清洗的势头和范围方面几乎享有全权。很快，这一行动获得了自身的动力，变成一台自行推进的机器：每一次逼供都导致新的“阴谋家”被牵连，而他们的供词又牵连更多人，如此以指数方式推进。当以这种方式被指控的人在各工作单位被捕时，他们余下的同事中有些人会告发别人，以显示自己的警惕，或谋取同事的职位。于是新的逮捕导致新的供词，又导致在不断扩散的恐慌中引出新的告发。而这一过程持续一年多以后，获得了一种连斯大林都觉得难以刹住的势头。
en: Stalin oversaw the operation at the highest level and often signed, together with other Politburo members, lists of people to be eliminated. But Ezhov and his NKVD staff actually carried out the purge, and they enjoyed pretty much carte blanche in determining its momentum and extent. Very soon the operation acquired a dynamic of its own and became a self-propelling mechanism: Each forced confession led to the incrimination of new “conspirators” whose confessions in turn incriminated still others, and so on in an exponential progression. As those accused in this manner were arrested in their various places of work some of their remaining colleagues would denounce others in order to demonstrate their own vigilance or to move into their colleagues’ jobs. Thus new arrests led to new confessions and then to new denunciations in ever widening circles of panic fear. And after this process had gone on for more than a year, it acquired a momentum that even Stalin found difficult to brake.

zh: 1937年3月至1939年初，深度政变吞没了中央委员会绝大多数成员、几乎所有1934年胜利者代表大会的代表、军官团的上层，以及大多数省和地方党委书记及其幕僚，还常常包括他们的家人。受害者要么未经公审被枪决，要么消失在古拉格。而由于党此时直接管理社会的一切部门——从经济、各部到艺术——国家专业干部的一大部分也消失了。因此结果是，到1939年，斯大林实际上已给自己提供了一个新党，以及在国民活动每个领域的一套新干部队伍。以其他方面衡量，大清洗无论多么不合理，这种制度巩固都是它的终极理据。斯大林此时拥有了他所建社会主义的人员。
en: Between March 1937 and early 1939, the coup-in-depth engulfed the overwhelming majority of Central Committee members, almost all former delegates to the Congress of Victors in 1934, the upper echelons of the officer corps, and most provincial and local Party secretaries, together with their staffs and very often their families. The victims either were shot without public trial or disappeared into the Gulag. And since the Party now directly managed all sections of society—from the economy and the ministries to the arts—a major part of the country’s professional cadres also disappeared. Thus it turned out that by 1939 Stalin had in effect given himself a new Party and a new corps of cadres in every field of national activity. This consolidation of the system was the ultimate rationale of the Great Purge, however irrational it was otherwise. Stalin now had the personnel of the socialism he had built.

zh: 这场新革命的突出特征是，1937年后被提拔到领导岗位的新人，几乎全都是1930年后所建制度的产物。此时留任要职的斯大林之前的人、或“旧人”已经很少——无论是旧资产阶级、老布尔什维克（即革命前入党的党员）、旧反对派，还是旧激进左派。新干部是第二次革命中向上流动的人，是五年计划的
），是对已建成的社会主义之前的世界几乎没有成年记忆的人，是在新制度下形成和受教育的人，是辩证唯物主义和社会主义现实主义文化世界的学生，是伟大领袖的忠实追随者，是将自己的一切归功于这一制度的缔造者斯大林同志的人。而正是这些人，在他们的领袖离开这个世界之后，将管理这个制度，直到它在1980年代末崩溃。
en: The outstanding characteristic of this new revolution was that almost all of the new men brought to the fore after 1937 were products of the system created after 1930. There were now very few pre-Stalin holdovers, or “former people”—whether old bourgeois, Old Bolsheviks (that is, Party members since before the Revolution), old oppositionists, or old militant Leftists—left in positions of responsibility. The new cadres were the upwardly mobile of the Second Revolution, the

of the Five-Year Plans, people who had little adult memory of the world that existed before built socialism, people who were formed and educated under the new system, pupils of the cultural world of dialectical materialism and socialist realism, devoted followers of the great Leader, people who owed everything to the architect of all this, Comrade Stalin. And these were the people who, after their Leader departed this world, would manage the system until it crumbled in the late 1980s.

zh: 所有这些人都是清洗相当直接的受益者，只要再瞥一眼尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫持续上升的仕途就可看出。
尽管他在中央的生涯起步要归功于卡冈诺维奇——后者最早把他从基辅带到莫斯科——但一到首都，赫鲁晓夫此后在党内的上升就直接归功于斯大林。1934年成为莫斯科党委书记后，他实际上充任斯大林管理该市的副手，而莫斯科的治理方式显然不同于其他城市中心。他还在1937年2—3月发动叶若夫时期的那次全会上支持老板，后来又组织街头示威，反对图哈切夫斯基元帅的罪行。
en: All of these people were quite directly the beneficiaries of the purges, as another glance at the continuing ascension of Nikita Khrushchev reveals.

Though he owed the beginning of his career at the center to Kaganovich, who first brought him from Kiev to Moscow, once in the capital Khrushchev owed his subsequent rise within the Party directly to Stalin. After becoming Moscow Party chairman in 1934, he functioned essentially as Stalin’s deputy for the administration of the city, which obviously was not governed in the same way that other urban centers were. He also supported the Boss at the February-March 1937 plenum that launched the
, and he later organized street demonstrations against the crimes of Marshal Tukhachevskii.

zh: 但赫鲁晓夫的宏大生涯直到1938年才开始，而且是乌克兰那场非同寻常的清洗的结果。在全联盟共产主义制度内，乌克兰党一直是一个半自治的封地，近乎一个公国，有点像军队。尽管乌克兰实际上是被布尔什维克征服的，其政府——第一任领导人是皮亚塔科夫——是党强加的，但地方机构久而久之变得对乌克兰民族情绪和利益作出回应。因此莫斯科定期派出新人员把事情拉回中央控制，然而每次之后，乌克兰又陷入旧错误。二十年代，卡冈诺维奇就是这样一个总督；三十年代扮演这一角色的是帕维尔·波斯蒂舍夫。尽管波斯蒂舍夫是一个无情的中央集权者，但他还是在1937年2—3月全会上主张缓和清洗。这成了他的覆灭之由，也是整个乌克兰党和政府的覆灭之由。
en: But Khrushchev’s grand career began only in 1938 and as a result of the extraordinary purge in Ukraine. The Ukrainian Party had always been a semiautonomous fief, almost a principality, within the All-Union Communist system, somewhat like the army. Although Ukraine had in fact been conquered by the Bolsheviks, and its government—whose first leader was Piatakov—had been imposed by the Party, in time the local apparat became responsive to Ukrainian national sentiment and interests. Moscow therefore periodically dispatched new personnel to bring things back under the center’s control, yet after each such occasion Ukraine relapsed into its old errors. In the twenties Kaganovich was such a satrap; in the thirties it was Pavel Postyshev who played that role. Although he was a ruthless centralizer, Postyshev nonetheless spoke for moderating the purge at the February-March 1937 plenum. And this was his undoing, as well as the undoing of the whole Ukrainian Party and government.

zh: 赫鲁晓夫、莫洛托夫、叶若夫和一列车的内务人民委员部部队被派往基辅去整顿地方机构，但乌克兰领导层拒绝合作。于是莫斯科决定对乌克兰一切结构进行彻底清洗：到1938年，乌克兰各级党政机构以及文化精英已被更换不止一次，而是两三次。那年1月，赫鲁晓夫被任命为“乌克兰”党中央第一书记，使命是建立一个全新的结构。同时，他当选为政治局候补委员，接替波斯蒂舍夫原来的席位；次年成为正式委员。他由此成为第二个较年轻的斯大林主义群体的领袖，该群体还包括1934年以来的文化沙皇日丹诺夫和未来的警察沙皇拉夫连季·贝利亚。
en: Khrushchev, Molotov, Ezhov, and a trainload of NKVD troops were dispatched to Kiev to prune the local apparat, but the Ukrainian leadership refused to cooperate. Moscow therefore decided on a clean sweep of all Ukrainian structures: By 1938 the Party and state apparats of Ukraine at all levels, as well as the cultural elite, had been replaced not once but twice or thrice. In January of that year Khrushchev was appointed first secretary of the “Ukrainian” Party, with the mission of building an entirely new structure. At the same time, he was elected to Postyshev’s old seat as a candidate member of the Politburo, and the next year he became a full member. He thus became a leader of the second, younger Stalinist group, which also included Zhdanov, the cultural tsar since 1934, and Lavrentii Beria, the future police tsar.

zh: 但在这个群体背后，而且正是由于他们执行老板旨意的努力，1937年后还有另一个斯大林主义世代在崛起。赫鲁晓夫需要新人来组建他的新乌克兰党，其中之一就是列昂尼德·勃列日涅夫。

像赫鲁晓夫一样，勃列日涅夫来自一个大俄罗斯人家庭，该家庭在旧制度末期迁往乌克兰从事工业。勃列日涅夫生于1906年，是第聂伯河畔钢铁城镇卡缅斯科耶一名工人的儿子。革命和内战时期，他还是一个不关心政治的青少年，在当地文理中学接受了一定程度的中等教育。到新经济政策开始时，他家人工作过的当地钢厂已经关闭。他迁回俄罗斯的家族原籍省份库尔斯克，1923年十七岁时在那里加入共青团，并进入一所职业学校学习成为测量员。在俄罗斯农村担任过若干职务后，到1931年他已回到卡缅斯科耶，在新成立的冶金学院学习，同时夜里在重新开工的钢厂上班，该厂此时以捷尔任斯基命名。简言之，他是斯大林的一名
，也是有抱负的新苏联工人知识分子的一员。同时，他此时二十五岁，入了党，并被指派负责他所在学院的共青团组织。那些日子里，乌克兰的党的积极分子经常被派往农村强制推行集体化，勃列日涅夫很可能也在其中。
en: But behind this group, and as a result of its efforts in carrying out the Boss’s behests, there was still another Stalinist generation on the rise after 1937. Khrushchev needed new men for his new Ukrainian Party, and one of them was Leonid Brezhnev.

Like Khrushchev, Brezhnev came from a Great Russian family that had been transplanted to Ukraine at the end of the Old Regime to work in industry. Born in 1906, Brezhnev was the son of a worker in the steel town of Kamenskoe on the Dnieper River. An apolitical adolescent at the time of the Revolution and the Civil War, he received something of a secondary education in the local gymnasium. By the beginning of the NEP the local steel mill where his family had worked had closed. He moved back to the family’s province of origin in Russia, Kursk, where in 1923, at age seventeen, he joined the Komsomol and entered a vocational school to become a surveyor. After occupying a number of posts in rural Russia, by 1931 he had returned to Kamenskoe, where he studied at the newly founded Metallurgical Institute while working nights at the reopened steel plant, now named for Dzerzhinskii. In short, he was one of Stalin’s

and an aspiring member of the new Soviet worker intelligentsia. At the same time, now twenty-five years of age, he entered the Party and was put in charge of the Komsomol organization of his Institute. In those days Party activists in Ukraine were regularly sent to the villages to impose collectivization, and in all probability Brezhnev was among them.

zh: 1934年从学院毕业成为工程师后，勃列日涅夫于1936年被任命为当地职业学校校长。接着，1937年，清洗席卷乌克兰。那年5月，勃列日涅夫接任了最近刚改名为第聂伯罗捷尔任斯克市苏维埃副主席这一空缺职位。次年，新任乌克兰第一书记赫鲁晓夫需要一千六百名党员填补共和国机构中的空缺，于是勃列日涅夫被任命为规模大得多的第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克州党委意识形态部部长。在这个职位上，他的职责是根除托洛茨基—布哈林—法西斯阴谋的一切表现，当然还有任何“乌克兰资产阶级民族主义”分子。于是一个完全斯大林主义的世代从清洗中崛起，继续从事人数日益减少的老斯大林派的工作——从莫洛托夫那一代年长者到较年轻的赫鲁晓夫一代，他们的生涯全都早于大跃进。
en: Having graduated from the Institute as an engineer in 1934, Brezhnev was made director of the local vocational school in 1936. Then, in 1937, the purge swept through Ukraine. In May of that year Brezhnev moved into the vacant job of vice chairman of the city soviet of what had recently been rebaptized Dneprodzerzhinsk. The next year the new Ukrainian First Secretary, Khrushchev, needed sixteen hundred Party members to fill empty posts in the republic’s apparat, so Brezhnev was named head of the Ideology Department in the provincial Party committee of the much larger city of Dnepropetrovsk. In this post his responsibility was to root out all manifestations of the Trotskyite-Bukharinite-fascist conspiracy and, of course, any elements of “Ukrainian bourgeois nationalism.” Thus a wholly Stalinist generation, emerged from the purges to continue the work of the dwindling number of older Stalinists, from the aged cohort of Molotov to that of the younger Khrushchev, all of whose careers antedated the Great Leap.

zh: 正如一位权威所说，这批年轻的斯大林主义者不妨称为“勃列日涅夫一代”。

在这一代人中，我们还可以找到安德烈·葛罗米柯、阿列克谢·柯西金、米哈伊尔·苏斯洛夫、尤里·安德罗波夫和康斯坦丁·契尔年科——也就是说，这些人将在赫鲁晓夫之后、直到戈尔巴乔夫上台之前统治俄国约三十年。这个群体卑微的出身和惊人的上升，被描述为社会向上流动的胜利；而众所周知，向上流动是一种民主现象。既然斯大林自下而上的“文化革命”也可以被赋予民主光环，他的革命现代化整体上就显得是进步的。于是苏联经验被概括为“恐怖、进步和社会流动”。

而且，在那些因斯大林政策而跻身名录干部的最高层的劳动之子们的崛起中，确实有一种粗略的社会民主；他们在那里度过了三十年的停滞岁月。但这种乐观评估建立在对1930年代非常片面的看法上，它只看到斯大林在工业化、城市化和教育方面的努力，却几乎忽略了集体化和大规模清洗，以及苏联式现代化必然带来的文化掺假。因此，聚焦社会流动的现代化理论变体，归结起来又是解决斯大林问题的另一种尝试。把记录中一个相当真实的方面即
）单独挑出，其余全部切除，我们就得到一个经过消毒的斯大林，可以舒舒服服地放进进步正典。但这个策略行不通，因为勃列日涅夫一代的上升与古拉格的大规模向下流动，两者重合得实在太令人不安。
en: As one authority put it, this new group of junior Stalinists may appropriately be called the “Brezhnev generation.”

In it we also find Andrei Gromyko, Aleksei Kosygin, Mikhail Suslov, Iurii Andropov, and Konstantin Chernenko—that is, the men who would rule Russia for some thirty years after Khrushchev and until the advent of Gorbachev. The humble origins and spectacular rise of this group have been described as a triumph of upward social mobility, and, as everyone knows, upward mobility is a democratic phenomenon. Since Stalin’s “cultural revolution” from below can also be given a democratic aura, his revolutionary modernization comes out looking progressive overall. Thus the Soviet experience has been summed up as “terror, progress, and social mobility.”
And, indeed, there was a rough social democracy involved in the rise of all those sons of toil who made it to the top of the

as a result of Stalin’s policies, and who stayed there for thirty stagnant years. But this cheery assessment rests on a very partial view of the 1930s, one that sees only Stalin’s efforts at industrialization, urbanization, and education, and that virtually ignores the collectivization and mass purging, as well as the adulteration of culture, that the Soviet manner of modernization necessarily entailed. That variant of the modernization theory that focuses on social mobility thus comes down to another attempt at solving the Stalin problem. By isolating one quite real aspect of the record,

, and amputating all the rest, we get a sanitized Stalin who fits comfortably into a canon of progress. But this stratagem does not work, for the rise of the Brezhnev generation coincides far too uncomfortably with the great downward mobility of the Gulag.

zh: 1929年之后的二十五年，也是苏联劳改营制度的大时代，它同样是集体化和清洗的产物。自从索尔仁尼琴的《古拉格群岛》以来，人们普遍知道，集中营制度不是始于斯大林，而是始于1918年列宁治下，当时在白海沿岸设有若干据点。这一制度在二十年代继续发展，尤其接收了许多宗教异见者。但它只有在1930年后流放富农时才变成一项庞大的体系。与此同时，它获得了重大的经济意义，因为强迫劳动被用来开发北部和西伯利亚其他不宜居住地区的自然资源——从木材、煤炭到钻石和黄金——政权认为在这些地方使用雇佣劳动过于昂贵。此外，营中的囚犯即
）还被用于斯大林一些钟爱的工程，如白海运河或莫斯科—伏尔加运河。甚至在莫斯科市内某些工程的铁丝网后面，也能看到
在工作。而且，古拉格制度从1930年起就是计划的常规部分。
en: The twenty-five years after 1929 were also the great age of the Soviet labor camp system, still another product of collectivization and the purges. Ever since Solzhenitsyn’s

, it has been common knowledge that the concentration camp system began not under Stalin but under Lenin in 1918 with various outposts along the White Sea. The system continued to grow during the twenties, receiving in particular many religious dissenters. But it became a gigantic operation only with the deportation of the kulaks after 1930. At the same time, it acquired major economic significance as forced labor was used to develop natural resources—from timber and coal to diamonds and gold—in inhospitable northern and other Siberian regions, where wage labor was considered too expensive by the regime. In addition, the inmates of the camps, the
, were employed on some of Stalin’s pet projects, such as the White Sea or Moscow-Volga canals.
could even be found working behind barbed wire on certain projects right in Moscow. The Gulag system, moreover, was a regular part of the Plan from 1930 onward.

zh: 古拉格在斯大林时代不断增长。它的第二次大征召，当然由清洗提供。第三次来自1939—1940年吞并的西部领土上的“资产阶级民族主义”分子。第四次注入源于第二次世界大战本身：掉队士兵、曾批评政权的军人（索尔仁尼琴只是最著名的案例），以及若干少数民族。第五次来自战争的胜利：在占领区与敌人合作、或曾被俘因而被归类为逃兵的苏联人。战后年代还有更多波次，因为营中死亡率很高，不断需要新的人。
en: The Gulag grew constantly throughout the Stalin years. Its second great levy, of course, was furnished by the purges. A third came from the “bougeois nationalist” elements in the western territories annexed in 1939-1940. A fourth infusion resulted from the Second World War itself: laggard soldiers, military personnel who had been critical of the regime (Solzhenitsyn is only the most famous case), and a number of minority nationalities. A fifth came from the victory in war: Soviets who had collaborated with the enemy in occupied territories or who had been taken prisoner and hence were classified as deserters. Other waves followed in the postwar years, for mortality rates were high in the camps, and new recruits were constantly needed.

zh: 营里有多少

？有多少人死在那里？清洗期间有多少人被处决？在这些问题上，确切的数字与同一时期苏联的经济增长率一样难以获得。当时显然没有关于这个问题的官方数据，而如今开放的苏联档案迄今也只被抽样。因此，我们手上的估计来自前劳改营囚犯的叙述和对人口普查数字的外推。这两种来源都足够不精确，为正当的辩论和分歧留下了相当大的空间——此外还必须加上一种潜意识的政治倾向：根据对苏维埃政权整体评价的不同，倾向于抬高或压低数字。
en: How many

were there in the camps? How many died there? How many were executed during the purges? Firm figures are as impossible to come by in these areas as are Soviet economic growth rates during the same period. There were obviously no official data on the subject at the time, and the now open Soviet archives have so far only been sampled. Thus the estimates that we have were derived from the accounts of former camp inmates and extrapolations from census figures. And both of these sources are sufficiently imprecise as to leave considerable latitude for legitimate debate and disagreement—to which must be added a subliminal political tendency to argue the figures up or down depending on one’s evaluation of the Soviet regime overall.

zh: 尽管如此，几十年来，关于所涉数量级已形成一个相当的公识。1930年代，外界大体上对清洗的规模或古拉格的存在一无所知。第二次世界大战后，当第一批
的叙述在西方出现时，

长期以来，相信它们是一件微妙的事，因为相信就等于把苏联等同于纳粹德国。直到赫鲁晓夫在1956年“秘密报告”中暗示清洗的席卷范围，然后又通过1962年授权出版索尔仁尼琴的《伊万·杰尼索维奇的一天》承认劳改营的存在，任何人才不再可能否认基本事实。此后辩论转向清洗的程度和古拉格的规模。然而，直到1968年罗伯特·康奎斯特的《大恐怖》（1968），尤其是索尔仁尼琴的《古拉格群岛》（1973—1975），才不容争辩地表明这两种现象都不是附带性的，而是核心性的。即便如此，直到1980年代，西方仍有许多人不愿正视这一问题，并重新断言苏联恐怖整个问题被大大夸大了。的确，一位较为极端的修正主义者提出了荒谬的主张，说清洗只杀死了“数千人”，监禁了“数万人”。
en: Nonetheless, over the decades a fair consensus has emerged as to the order of magnitude involved. In the 1930s the outside world by and large knew nothing about the scope of the purges or the existence of the Gulag. After the Second World War, when the first accounts by
appeared in the West,

it was for a long time a delicate matter to give them credence, because to do so implied equating the Soviet Union with Nazi Germany. It was only after Khrushchev hinted at the sweep of the purges in his “secret speech” of 1956, and then acknowledged the existence of the camps by authorizing the publication of Solzhenitsyn’s

Nonetheless, it is still difficult, and may be forever impossible, to give firm and precise figures. The initial difficulty in giving a realistic estimate of the scale of the purges lies in defining what one considers a purge loss.

zh: 第一，有一类界限明确的处决。这些处决常常由特别会议、特别法庭和完全非法的“三人小组”即席下令，后者由地方党委第一书记、一名内务人民委员部军官和地区检察官组成。此外还有涉及数千受害者的大规模处决，如1940年在卡廷森林屠杀波兰军官，或1939年在明斯克附近库罗帕蒂屠杀苏联平民。
en: First, there is the clear-cut category of executions. These were often summarily ordered by special councils, special tribunals, and wholly extra-legal “troikas” composed of the local Party First Secretary, an NKVD officer, and the district prosecutor. In addition, there were mass executions involving thousands of victims, such as the Katyn Forest massacre of Polish officers in 1940 or the slaughter of Soviet civilians at Kuropaty near Minsk in 1939.

zh: 第二，有一类更有弹性的死亡，即因监狱和劳改营条件而死亡，以及与此相关的两处机构的囚禁人数问题。惩罚有不同等级，从北极或科雷马河谷的苦役营（它们常常为计划采矿或伐木），到把整个民族如车臣—印古什人流放到中亚，再到把富农有时罚往西伯利亚没有围墙的“定居点”这种较温和的流放。还有一个问题是劳改营人口的寿命，从而也是囚犯的更替率——以及它逐年变化的情况。在认真审查劳改营制度现存档案证据之前，我们关于其性质最有力的证词是文学性的，如索尔仁尼琴的《古拉格》或瓦尔拉姆·沙拉莫夫的《科雷马故事》。古拉格没有留下实体遗迹，也没有作为死者纪念碑保存下来的营地。整个制度在赫鲁晓夫治下被推土机推入地下。
en: Second, there is the more elastic category of deaths from the conditions in prison and camps, and the related matter of the number of those incarcerated in both institutions. There were different levels of punishment, ranging from hard-labor camps in the arctic or the Kolyma valley (which were often engaged in mining or cutting lumber for the Plan), to the deportation to Central Asia of whole nationalities, such as the Chechen-Ingush, to the milder forms of exile to unenclosed “settlements” in Siberia that were at times inflicted on kulaks. There is also the question of the longevity, and consequently of the inmate turnover, of the camp population—and its variations from year to year. Pending serious examination of what archival evidence remains of the camp system, our most telling testimony about its nature is literary, such as Solzhenitsyn’s
or Varlam Shalamov’s
. There are no physical remains of the Gulag, or camps that have been preserved as memorials to the dead. The entire system was bulldozed into the ground under Khrushchev.

zh: 最后，还有一个更困难的问题：处决和劳改营制度造成的死亡所带来的出生缺口。而这个问题又涉及被清洗人口所出自的人口基数。1937年的人口普查是1926年以来第一次，它显示比预期人口增长少了六百万，这一缺口显然由集体化和清洗造成。作为回应，斯大林压制了普查，枪杀了人口普查负责人，并下令1939年进行新普查，得出了更“令人满意”但明显伪造的结果。尽管1937年普查现已公布，重建这一时期人口史的任务仍然艰巨。
en: Finally, there is the still more difficult question of the deficit in births arising as a byproduct of deaths due to executions and the camp system. And this question raises the matter of the demographic pool from which the purged population was drawn. The census of 1937, the first since 1926, revealed a deficit from anticipated population growth of six million, a shortfall obviously caused by the collectivization and the purges. In response, Stalin suppressed the census, had the census takers shot, and ordered a new census made in 1939 which yielded more “satisfactory” but clearly falsified results. Even though the 1937 census has now been published, the task of reconstructing the demographic history of the period remains a difficult one.

zh: 然而，尽管这批证据纠缠不清且不充分，浮现出来的斯大林时代俄国图景，仍是本世纪任何时期、任何国家中最阴惨的。总体而言，1926—1939年的人口缺口大约为一千五百万，主要在村庄。1939—1950年（这一时期包括第二次世界大战的并行灾难）的人口缺口大约为五千五百万，其中一半是出生缺口，一半是超额死亡。在计算人口总损失时，还必须包括战争期间的一两百万移民。
en: Yet despite the tangled and inadequate nature of this body of evidence, the picture that emerges of the Stalin era in Russia is the grimmest of any period or country in this century. In global terms, the demographic deficit for the years 1926-1939 is probably fifteen million, mostly in the villages. The demographic deficit for the years 1939-1950 (a period which includes the parallel catastrophe of the Second World War) is probably fifty-five million, one-half of it a shortfall in births and one-half an excess of deaths. In computing the total loss in population one must also include one or two million émigrés during the war.

zh: 至于劳改营中的实际死亡人数，康奎斯特给出1938年

为八百万；他把这个数字当作1936至1950年间每年的平均劳改营人口，并假定每年至少有10%的劳改营人口死亡，由此估计这一时期总共有约一千二百万死亡。在此基础上还必须加上1937—1939年恐怖高峰时约一百万起处决。最后，如果加上集体化受害者的较低估计六百万，我们得到斯大林整个统治时期因政治原因死亡的总数接近两千万。经济学家亚历克·诺夫的更谨慎计算，也得出了斯大林主义代价的类似估计。而两千万这个数字现在是俄罗斯最广泛接受的。
en: To turn to actual deaths in the camps, Conquest gives the figure of eight million

as of 1938; taking this as the average camp population for each of the years between 1936 and 1950, and assuming that at least 10 percent of the camp population died each year, he estimates that there was a total of some twelve million deaths in this period. To this must be added around a million executions at the height of the Terror in 1937-1939. Finally, if we add the lower estimate for the victims of collectivization, six million, we get a grand total approaching twenty million deaths from political causes for all of Stalin’s reign. Economist Alec Nove, in his more cautious computations, arrives at comparable estimations of the cost of Stalinism. And the figure of twenty million is now the most widely accepted in Russia.

zh: 这个数字是第一次世界大战全部损失的两倍，与苏联在第二次世界大战中的损失大致相同。因此它是历史上最大的一次恐怖收成。而在这场人类恐怖之外，还必须加上一个物质事实：古拉格是一项极其浪费的经济事业，甚至比集体化更糟：1938年的八百万

en: This figure is twice the number of all losses in the First World War, and approximately the same as the Soviet losses in the Second World War. As such it is the largest single harvest of terror in history. And to this human horror must be added the material fact that the Gulag was a monumentally wasteful economic enterprise, even worse than collectivization: The eight million
of 1938 represented 9 percent of the Soviet adult population.

zh: 正是在古拉格的这个高峰年1938年，恐怖的种种危险开始对政权变得明显。于是，叶若夫被配了一名副手拉夫连季·贝利亚，清洗放慢了速度。特别是贝利亚通过引入
即精英劳改营制度，缓冲了古拉格的浪费，那里有高度合格的人员为军方从事研究项目。叶若夫很快被调到水运人民委员部，次年贝利亚完全接管后他就消失了。对叶若夫从未有过任何审判，甚至没有公开谴责，但内务人民委员部首脑的更替是一个信号：大恐怖结束了。
en: It was in this peak year of the Gulag, 1938, that the dangers of the terror began to become apparent to the regime. Accordingly, Ezhov was given a deputy, Lavrentii Beria, and the purge was slowed down. In particular, Beria cushioned the wastefulness of the Gulag by introducing the institution of the

, or elite camp, where highly qualified personnel worked on research projects for the military. Ezhov was soon moved to the Commissariat of Water Transport, and then disappeared the following year when Beria took over completely. There was never any trial, or even public condemnation, of Ezhov, but the change of NKVD chiefs was a signal that the Great Terror was over.

zh: 然而这并不意味着一切恐怖都停止了。相反，在贝利亚治下，恐怖与古拉格一起被常规化，成为制度的组成部分。1936年以前，苏联是一个潜伏着警察威胁的社会，但并不是无处不在的警察在场意义上的警察国家。它也不是一个彻底被恐怖统治的社会，这也是斯大林能够搞成清洗的原因之一：党和民众根本不能相信像叶若夫时期这样的事是可能的，因此完全措手不及。然而1937年后，苏联成了一个被恐怖统治的警察国家。尽管内务人民委员部的全部权力没有公开宣传，古拉格也完全未被提及，但人人都知道这些机构的作用，因而处处小心谨慎。这个国家被上了一堂沉重的课，从此以后，苏联在很大程度上靠恐惧统治。
en: This does not mean, however, that all terror ceased. Rather, under Beria it was routinized, along with the Gulag, as an integral part of the system. Before 1936 the Soviet Union had been a society with a lurking police threat, but it had not been a police state in the sense of a ubiquitous police presence. Nor had it been a thoroughly terrorized society, which is one of the reasons why Stalin could get away with the purges: The Party and the population simply could not believe that anything like the

was possible, and so they were taken completely unaware. After 1937, however, the Soviet Union was a terrorized police state. Although no publicity was given to the full power of the NKVD, and the Gulag was not mentioned at all, everyone was aware of the role of these institutions and so behaved with appropriate caution. The country had been taught a mighty lesson, and from this time onward the Soviet Union was ruled in large measure by fear.

en: THE CUNNING OF UNREASON

zh: 那么，当我们纵览斯大林主义清洗与巩固的全景——从文化国有化到公审，从党干部更换和对乌克兰的政变到西伯利亚的劳改营——关于这场剧变的更深层原因，能做出哪些可信的概括？再者，斯大林个人与制度总体动力在这一过程中的相对作用又是什么？
en: So when we survey the whole scene of Stalinist purge and consolidation—from the nationalization of culture to the show trials, from the replacement of Party cadres and the coup against Ukraine to the Siberian camps—what plausible generalizations can be made about the deeper causes of this upheaval? And, again, what were the relative roles of Stalin the individual and of the system’s overall dynamics in this process?

zh: 尽管斯大林显然是这场剧变中每一事件的发动者，但这并不意味着他是戏剧中

），一个外在于制度、把制度拨离其自然轨道的因素。1937年以前也没有迹象表明他正在失去对自己或对局势的控制。只有在1937—1938年，他的多疑似乎越界进入病态，例如他公开宣称没有人可以信任，或者那些最热心揭露人民敌人的人，实际上可能只是在掩盖自己的叛国。然而即便在这种多疑的发作中，他也从未攻击党最高层长期忠诚的核心骨干，因为这些人对他对整个党发动政变是必要的。他政治局的老伙伴莫洛托夫、卡冈诺维奇和伏罗希洛夫，或者次一级的较新人如日丹诺夫、赫鲁晓夫或贝利亚，看来几乎没有什么可害怕的。
在这个最高群体中，斯大林唯一触动的人物是那些积极抵抗政变的人，如奥尔忠尼启则，或可能是国家计委主席瓦列里安·古比雪夫，后者1935年的死亡方便得可疑。然而在1938年，斯大林清洗了五名二级政治局委员——主要与乌克兰问题有关——这使他接近了对自己指挥结构的真正危险边缘。这一步，加上工业管理者和军队中失控的大批消灭，终于使他回头，也许是最高副手们催促的结果，并通过用贝利亚取代叶若夫来稳定恐怖。
en: Although Stalin was clearly the initiator of each event in the upheaval, this does not mean that he was the

of the drama, an agent external to the system who deflected it from its natural course. Nor were there signs before 1937 that he was losing control either of himself or of the situation. Only in 1937-1938 did his suspiciousness seem to cross the border into the pathological, as in his public declarations that no one could be trusted, or that those most zealous in unmasking enemies of the people might in fact be only covering up their own treason. Yet even in this paroxysm of suspicion he never attacked the hard core of long-time stalwarts at the top of the Party who were necessary to the carrying out of his coup against the Party as a whole. His old Politburo cronies, Molotov, Kaganovich, and Voroshilov, or, at the next level, newer men like Zhdanov, Khrushchev, or Beria, seem to have had little to fear.

The only figures in this top group whom Stalin touched were men who actively resisted the coup, such as Ordzhonikidze, or possibly the head of Gosplan, Valerian Kuibyshev, whose death in 1935 was suspiciously convenient. In 1938, however, Stalin approached the threshold of real danger to his own command structure when he purged five second-rank Politburo members, principally in connection with the Ukrainian matter. This step, in conjunction with the runaway decimations among industrial managers and the military, at last caused him to turn back, perhaps prodded by his chief lieutenants, and to stabilize the terror by replacing Ezhov with Beria.

zh: 此外，到这时政变已实现其政治目标。因为，重复一遍，在苏联此时已变成的超现实世界中，有些政治目标具有反常的意义。总目标已经提到，即给党提供它所建社会主义的人员。诚然，清洗受害者的绝大多数——从奥尔忠尼启则、皮亚塔科夫到无数地方党委书记和军官团成员——都是忠诚的斯大林派，本会无限期地继续为领袖及其政策服务。从实际角度说，大规模取代他们不仅无助于制度更好地运转，而且确实有害，尤其鉴于战争迫近的可能性。但所有这些人尽管经过多年灌输，还不是制度的被动齿轮；他们在制度建立过程中出于信念支持它，并保留着残余的批判思考和回嘴能力——波斯蒂舍夫的例子就是明证。简言之，他们还不是成熟制度所需要、文化国有化本应造就的“苏维埃新人”。毕竟，斯大林在把布哈林送上被告席的同时，也为《简明教程》做了最后润色。
en: Moreover, by this time the coup had achieved its political objectives. For, to repeat, there were political objectives that made perverse sense in the surreal world the Soviet Union had now become. The overall objective has already been mentioned, namely, to give the Party the personnel of the socialism it had built. To be sure, the vast majority of the purge victims—from Ordzhonikidze and Piatakov to innumerable local Party secretaries and members of the officer corps—were loyal Stalinists who would have continued to serve the Leader and his policies indefinitely. To replace them en masse was not only unnecessary to make the system function better in practical terms, it was indeed downright harmful, especially in view of the looming possibility of war. But all these men, despite years of indoctrination, were not yet passive cogs of the system; they had supported it out of conviction as it was being built, and they retained a vestigial capacity for critical thought and talking back—the example of Postyshev is a case in point. In short, they were not yet the “new Soviet men” that the mature system required and that the nationalization of culture had been intended to produce. at the same time he put Bukharin in the dock.

zh: 这一情况解释了清洗的另一个政治目标：在新文化的力量被证明不足的情况下，用制度化的恐怖和靠恐惧统治来支撑它。但要解释这一策略，我们不必求助于苏维埃主义的独特性质，更不必求助于斯大林的心理。有意识地以恐怖进行社会控制的政策，在二十世纪政治中太常见地成为一个“理性”目标。苏维埃制度只是把它推到了极致。
en: And this circumstance explains another political objective of the purge: In cases where the power of the new culture proved insufficient, it would be backed up by institutionalized terror and rule through fear. But to explain this tactic we do not need to have re-course to the unique nature of Sovietism or, still less, to Stalin’s psyche. A deliberate policy of social control by terror has been all too frequently a “rational” goal in twentieth-century politics. The Soviet system simply carried this to its ultimate extreme.

zh: 大恐怖更具苏联特色的方面，可以从其展开过程中的两个谜团看出。第一，所有清洗受害者都被要求供认他们并未犯下、而且他们的内务人民委员部审讯者知道他们并未犯下的罪行。第二，制度各级中任何一位神志无疑正常的人，都没有试图抵抗这整场荒诞的假面剧。
en: A more uniquely Soviet aspect of the Great Terror is revealed by two mysteries in the manner of its unfolding. The first is that all of the victims of the purge were required to confess to crimes that they had not committed and that their NKVD interrogators knew they had not committed. The second is that none of the indubitably sane people at any level of the system attempted to resist the whole fantastic charade.

zh: 人们如何被迫招供，这并不神秘：他们要么屈服于酷刑，要么屈服于对其家人的威胁。政权为什么用这些手段让三次公审中的被告公开重复供词，也并不神秘。这些供词对于教育民众认识叛徒和破坏者的遍及各地的阴谋、从而激发一场全国警惕运动是必要的。更耐人寻味、也更重要的是这样一个事实：成千上万——很可能是数十万——的“敌人”在内务人民委员部监狱紧闭的门后被逼签署供词，这些供词从未公布，签署者被悄悄枪决或送往古拉格。无数工时被耗费在对民众没有教育价值的活动上，而内务人民委员部本可以伪造文件，或者干脆不经供词就枪决这些“敌人”。
en: There is no mystery as to how people were made to confess: They either succumbed to torture or to threats against their families. Nor is there any mystery as to why the regime used these means to bring the accused in the three show trials to repeat their confessions in public. These confessions were necessary to educate the population about the universal plot of traitors and wreckers, and so to stimulate a national campaign of vigilance. Much more intriguing and important is the fact that many tens, and probably hundreds, of thousands of “enemies” were made to sign confessions behind the closed doors of NKVD prisons, confessions that were never made public and whose authors were quietly shot or shipped off to the Gulag. Untold manhours were expended on activity without pedagogical value for the population, when the NKVD could have forged the documents or simply shot these “enemies” without a confession.

zh: 这种显然荒谬之谜，也许可以通过与纳粹做法的比较来澄清。纳粹不需要悔过，只用暴力碾碎敌人。苏维埃和纳粹政权实际上都依靠武力，但各自运用方式大不相同。纳粹集中营大体上是为非德国人准备的，政权的侵略指向其他民族。苏联劳改营首先是给苏联公民的，政权首先向国内“阶级敌人”开战。纳粹的意识形态是相对简单的意志与武力意识形态，因此他们可以公开宣布其侵略和惩罚意图。苏联更复杂的意识形态为阶级斗争的暴力留出了充分余地，但仍在形式上使之从属于合理进步和人道的促进；因此他们不能公开承认自己的统治基本上依靠武力。于是苏联人必须让他们的“敌人”供认犯罪行为，从而承认对他们的消灭是公正而应得的。同样，这些敌人的动机也被恶毒地贬低。纳粹集中营则不必费心搞供词。
en: The mystery of this apparent absurdity may be clarified by a comparison with the practices of the Nazis, who had no need of recantations but simply crushed their enemies by brute force. Both the Soviet and the Nazi regimes in fact rested on force, but each applied it quite differently. The Nazi concentration camps were by and large for non-Germans, and the regime’s aggression was directed against other nations. Soviet camps were above all for Soviet citizens, and the regime made war first of all against domestic “class enemies.” The Nazis’ ideology was a relatively simple ideology of will and force; therefore they could openly proclaim their aggressive and punitive intentions. The Soviets’ more complex ideology made ample allowance for the violence of class struggle but nonetheless formally subordinated this to the promotion of rational progress and humanity; therefore they could not publicly admit that their rule rested basically on force. It was thus necessary for the Soviets to make their “enemies” confess to criminal actions and thereby recognize their elimination as just and deserved. By the same token, the motivation of these enemies was viciously debased. Nazi camps did not bother with confessions.

zh: 这就是维辛斯基在公审中针对“疯狗”的辞令所传达的信息，也是苏联报刊不断警告有人阴谋“复辟资本主义”所传达的信息。但内务人民委员部的审讯者在紧闭的门后使用同样的语言，而他们和受害者都知道那是骗人的。然而，这种做法的荒谬不应使我们把它当作毫无意义而摒弃。它的政治目的是让民众被迫卷入政权的意识形态目标。
于是第二次革命的受害者被迫成为自己毁灭的共谋，从而既赦免了政权的罪行，又庆祝了其政策的胜利。而且，尽管这场假面剧没有公开，但党内和苏联精英中已普遍知道，人人都必须这样确认大阴谋的存在。人们不必相信这个阴谋，但必须假装相信。
en: This was the message of Vyshinskii’s rhetoric against “mad dogs” in the show trials, and of the incessant warnings of the Soviet press against the great plot to “restore capitalism.” But the same language was used by the NKVD’s interrogators behind closed doors, where both they and their victims knew it was fraudulent. The absurdity of this exercise, however, should not lead us to dismiss it as meaningless. Its political purpose was to compromise the population in the ideological aims of the regime.

So the victims of the Second Revolution were forced to become accomplices in their own undoing, thereby both absolving the regime of its crimes and celebrating the victory of its policies. And, although this charade was not made public, it became generally known within the Party and among the Soviet elite that such confirmation of the great plot’s existence was required of all. People did not have to believe in the plot, but they did have to pretend they believed.

zh: 此外，这一现象与其他苏联做法有关。它最一般的形式是“自我批评”制度，一种仪式，犯错的同志必须在党的会议前承认错误并拥护“正确”路线。或者它类似于集体化期间的村民大会，农民必须谴责“富农危险”，仿佛这种危险真的存在于农民之中。最后，清洗中的供认类似于斯大林宪法下举行定期而无意义选举的做法，在那种选举中，99%的人口投票支持“党和非党候选人名单”。就理性政治而言，这一切都毫无意义。但在已建成社会主义的意识形态统治世界中，它有一种古怪的意义。1937年后斯大林也许有点疯了——然而这个制度肯定是疯了。
en: This phenomenon, moreover, is related to other Soviet practices. Its most general form is the institution of “self-criticism,” a ritual whereby delinquent comrades were made to confess their errors and to subscribe to the “correct” line before a Party meeting. Or it is similar to village meetings during collectivization, when peasants had to denounce the “kulak danger” as if such a danger really existed for the peasantry. Finally, the purge confession is analogous to the practice of holding regular and meaningless elections under the Stalin Constitution, elections in which 99 percent of the population voted for the “list of Party and non-Party candidates.” In terms of rational politics all of this is senseless. But in the ideocratic world of built socialism, it made an odd sort of sense. After 1937 Stalin may have been somewhat mad—the system, however, most certainly was.

zh: 清洗的第二个大谜团是，为什么党内没有人试图抵抗。当然，党外对斯大林革命有过抵抗：所谓的富农曾反击，但更多是出于绝望，而不是抱有胜利希望；工人常常刺杀斯达汉诺夫分子，实际上把他们当作抬高工作定额的“工贼”。但在自上而下恐怖统治的十年中，对政权领袖的唯一暴力行为是尼古拉耶夫刺杀基洛夫。然而，广大民众的无助很容易解释：政权对军事和警察权力的垄断如此彻底，社会中没有任何分子有机会对抗它。在这一点上，俄国案例并不独特：在其他极权国家，组织抵抗同样不可能。更难理解的是，为什么党、警察和军队各自都有斗争手段，却如此温顺地屈服，甚至配合自己的毁灭。
en: The second major mystery of the purges is why no one in the Party attempted to resist. There had, of course, been resistance to the Stalin revolution outside the Party: The so-called kulaks had fought back, but more in despair than out of any hope of victory; and workers had often assassinated Stakhanovites as, in effect, “scabs” who forced work norms upwards. But in a decade of terror from above, the only act of violence against a leader of the regime was Nikolaev’s assassination of Kirov. The helplessness of the population at large, however, is easily explained by the fact that the regime’s monopoly of military and police power was such that no elements in society stood a chance against it. And in this the Russian case is not unique: It was equally impossible in other totalitarian states to organize resistance. What is less understandable is why the Party, the police, and the military, each having access to means of struggle, submitted so meekly and indeed cooperated in their own destruction.

zh: 原因是，他们被制度的性质以及它多年获得的势头弄瘫痪了。他们都是那套逻辑的囚徒；皮亚塔科夫附和托洛茨基，曾夸口说这套逻辑就是他的：“如果党要求……我会把本以为看到白色的地方看成黑色……因为对我来说，党之外没有生活。”到1930年代后期，这种心态已使他们丧失一切组织或集体行动的能力。此外还必须加上一个事实：这些党、警察和军队人员多年来一直参与对民众的系统性暴力，因此当暴力转向他们时，他们没有道德上的理由反对。
en: The reason is that they were paralyzed by the nature of the system and by the momentum it had acquired over the years. They were all prisoners of the logic that Piatakov, echoing Trotsky, boasted was his: “If the Party demands it … I will see black where I thought I saw white … because for me there is no life outside the Party.” By the late 1930s this mentality had deprived them of all capacity to organize or act collectively. To this must be added the fact that these same Party, police, and military personnel had for years engaged in systematic violence against the population and therefore were without moral defense for objecting when violence was turned against them.

zh: 此外，他们都纵容了一系列政治清洗，这些清洗逐步把容许异见的范围逐步缩小到零。先是君主主义者和自由派被禁，接着是孟什维克和社会革命党人，然后是托洛茨基分子和布哈林分子；而随着每一个群体的消失，消灭下一个就变得更容易。因此在这一过程结束时，如果党内仅存的权威即领袖宣布斯大林主义的布尔什维克此时也已成为“反党”力量，那就没有理由不把他们也清洗掉。因此，清洗是从列宁把一切非布尔什维克政治谴责为“小资产阶级”政治——即只配被消灭的阶级敌人的政治——这一逻辑的终点。
en: Moreover, they had all condoned a succession of political purges that had progressively narrowed the range of dissent to zero. First the monarchists and liberals had been proscribed, then the Mensheviks and SRs, and then the Trotskyites and Bukharinites; and with the disappearance of each group, it became easier to eliminate the next. Thus at the end of the process there was no reason why Stalinist Bolsheviks should not also be purged if the only remaining authority in the Party, the Leader, declared that they, too, had now become an “anti-Party” force. The purges therefore are the end point of the logic that began with Lenin’s condemnation of all non-Bolshevik politics as “petty-bourgeois,” that is, the politics of a class enemy fit only to be destroyed.

zh: 但这一顶点并不意味着安全警察此时已取代党成为制度的核心，如斯大林的继承人后来所断言的那样，以解释他们当时为何未能抵抗。

斯大林此时利用警察统治党，正如他一直利用党统治国家。但他做这一切时是作为党的化身，而不是仅仅作为警察的首脑。后一项任务，他有可以牺牲的叶若夫或奴颜婢膝的贝利亚。斯大林必须保持党的至高地位，因为党是政权意识形态目的的化身，从而是其合法性的基础。否则，他何必费心写一章辩证唯物主义并强加给全国所有学校？这样的国家不可能像斯特罗斯纳将军的巴拉圭那样，被交给警察的肆意控制。它生来就是一个意识形态统治的党治，因此只要它存在，就必须保持如此。
en: But this culmination does not mean that the security police had now replaced the Party as the heart of the system, as Stalin’s heirs later asserted to explain why they failed to resist at the time.

Stalin now used the police to rule the Party, just as he had always used the Party to rule the country. But he did all of this as the embodiment of the Party, not as the mere head of the police. For the latter task he had the expendable Ezhov or the servile Beria. Stalin had to keep the Party supreme because it was the embodiment of the ideological purpose of the regime, and therefore the basis of its legitimacy. Otherwise, why should he bother to write a chapter on dialectical materialism and force it on all the schools of the country? Such a country could not be delivered over to the unbridled control of the police as if it were the Paraguay of General Stroessner. It had been born, and therefore had to remain as long as it survived, an ideocratic partocracy.

zh: 因此，清洗和恐怖的制度化完成了党对市民社会的粉碎，以及人口的近乎原子化。面对党国，此时只存在一个苍白的影子社会和一大批孤立个人，他们害怕彼此交往，甚至被胜利社会主义的新文化约束得不敢想这样做。曼德尔施塔姆是最早描述这个新世界的人之一：“我们生活在一个变得不真实而陌生的国度；十步之外，没人听得见我们的交谈。”
en: The purges and the institutionalization of terror thus completed the Party’s pulverization of civil society and the near-atomization of the population. Vis-à-vis the Party-state there now existed only a palid shadow society and a mass of isolated individuals afraid to associate among themselves and constrained even from thinking of doing so by the new culture of socialism triumphant. Mandelshtam was one of the first to describe this new world: “We exist in a land grown unreal and strange, / Ten steps away no one hears the talk we exchange.”

zh: 人口通过发展一种双层意识、或一种永久精神分裂式的视野来适应新形势。知识分子尤其如此，尽管工人也受影响，而农民也许受影响最小。一般来说，年轻人照字面接受政权的神话，而他们的长辈通常不愿冒险打破他们的幻想。然而随着人变老，他们更充分地意识到神话与现实之间的差距，但他们知道这不能公开承认。因此，作为公开的社会人，他们拥护官方世界观，说它那套生硬语言，甚至在一定程度上相信它。但作为私下的个人，他们使用正常逻辑和人类语言，同时从未完全否定官方世界观。只有付出这种心理分隔、或用奥威尔的话说“双重思想（
）”的代价，个人神志才能在一个此时处于谵妄凯旋顶点的制度中得以保全。
en: The population adapted to this new situation by developing a two-tiered consciousness, or a permanently schizophrenic vision. This was particularly true of the intelligentsia, though the workers were also affected, while the peasants were probably touched least of all. In general terms, the young accepted the myths of the regime at face value, and their elders usually would not take the risk of disabusing them. As people grew older, however, they realized more fully the gap between the myth and the reality, yet they knew that this could not be acknowledged openly. So as public, social persons they subscribed to the official view of the world, spoke its wooden language, and even half-believed it. But as private, individual persons they used normal logic and human language, while never wholly repudiating the official worldview. It was only at the price of this psychological compartmentalization or, in Orwell’s term, doublethink that personal sanity could be preserved amidst a system now at the triumphant pinnacle of delirium.

zh: 然而，正是这一凯旋为制度的最终瓦解创造了条件。清洗之后，现实与理想之间的差距甚至比社会主义在十年中期首次实现时更大。此时只有服务于一种超现实阴谋理论的永久恐怖，才能弥合这一差距。与此同时，党的意识形态合法性已完全集中到领袖个人身上。整个大厦是一项独特而非凡的成就。但它也是一项非常脆弱的成就。
en: Nonetheless, this very triumph had created the conditions for the system’s ultimate undoing. After the purges, the gap between reality and the ideal was even greater than it had been when socialism was first achieved in the mid-decade. This gap could now be bridged only by permanent terror in the service of a surreal conspiracy theory. Concomitantly, the ideocratic legitimacy of the Party had been wholly absorbed into the person of the Leader. The whole edifice was a unique and extraordinary achievement. But it was also a very fragile one.

zh: 因为把政权的意识形态目的化约为这些粗糙简单的表述，已开始摧毁政权所赖以存在的基础。成熟时期的斯大林主义这些非同寻常的转变的最终后果是，它们的源头即社会主义神话，此时已变成苏联谎言——用这个最早由索尔仁尼琴引起公众注意、但早已在东欧普遍流行的说法。因为实际实现的苏联社会主义，按神话自身的标准就是一场骗局。只要神话—谎言的活化身仍然掌权，整个惊人的结构就能维持在一起。但他作为领袖的凯旋本身，也将给他的党、更给他的人民留下一张在未来几十年必须支付的极其沉重的账单。
en: For the reduction of the ideological purpose of the regime to these crude and simple expressions was beginning to destroy the basis on which the regime rested. The ultimate consequence of the extraordinary transformations of high Stalinism was that their source, the Socialist Myth, had now been transformed into the Soviet Lie, to use a term that was first brought to public attention by Solzhenitsyn but that had long been current throughout Eastern Europe. For Soviet socialism as actually realized was a fraud in terms of the Myth’s own standards. So long as the living embodiment of the Myth-Lie remained in power, the whole astounding structure would hold together. But his very triumph as Leader would also leave an inordinately heavy bill for his Party and, even more, for his people to pay over the ensuing decades.
